positions.text: DAO governance must be assessed at the level of power allocation and execution exposure, not only procedural form. A voting process does not establish decentralization when purchasable influence, delegation concentration, or automatic execution leave governance open to capture.
scope_conditions: DAO governance systems where influence can be purchased or concentrated through delegation, or where formally valid votes can trigger automatic execution.

current_debate.name: On Exercising Governance Power in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations

extends.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783

positions.text: MCP governance should be treated as a continuous institutional process, not as a sequence of static releases. Discovery, authorization, tool permissions, and observed failure data require an auditable review mechanism that can adapt rules without erasing accountability.
scope_conditions: MCP discovery, authorization, tool permission, and protocol governance where behavior data and auditable review are available.

extends.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How can we Best Monitor AI Agents (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5245185
extends.paper: How can we Best Monitor AI Agents

positions.text: Agentic AI governance should be organized around action level accountability. A governance roadmap is incomplete unless it can reconstruct the agent action, delegated mandate, evidence used, review path, and downstream effect.
scope_conditions: Agentic AI systems with delegated authority where actions, evidence, review, and downstream effects can be recorded.

current_debate.name: Towards Agentic AI Governance: A Preliminary Assessment
